facts.text: TaskSchedulingEnv subclasses gymnasium.Env: it is the Gymnasium interface of the benchmark
The number of datacenters is read from the cluster manager (self.num_dcs = len(...))
One simulation step advances the clock by 15 minutes (pd.Timedelta(minutes=15))
In single-action mode with deferral disabled, the action space is Discrete(num_dcs)
With deferral disabled, an agent action 0..N-1 is shifted by one and assigned to datacenter 1..N
The aggregated observation dimension is 4 time features + 5 aggregated task features + 5 features per datacenter
The time features are the sine and cosine of the day of year and of the hour of day
The per-task features are origin datacenter id, cores, GPUs, duration and minutes to the SLA deadline
The datacenter features are available/total cores, GPUs and memory, carbon intensity/1000 and price/100
reset(seed) increments the episode count, seeds Python's random generator and the cluster manager, and returns (observation, info)
step returns (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info) after advancing the clock and loading the next tasks
An episode is done and truncated when current_time reaches end_time
The reward is 0.0 when the environment is constructed without a reward function
The shipped simulation config enables single_action_mode and disable_defer_action
The README documents a Gymnasium-compatible environment interface for RL agents
The README documents the simulation timestep as 15 minutes

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reseeds the environment's task generator (envs/task_scheduling_env.py:239-241) and the fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream also seeds its cluster manager, and the fake was never compared with the upstream environment

gaps: kinematic/analytic model (F0): the environment advances a scheduler clock and state transitions, not rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators or sensors

the fake backend models one fixed five-datacenter test configuration and generates placeholder tasks; it does not run DatacenterClusterManager, SustainDC, the workload trace, the reward engine or the energy, carbon and thermal models
upstream needs pandas, numpy, torch and the Alibaba workload dataset; nothing was installed or run, so the fake was never compared with the upstream environment
no rendering, no snapshot and no restore: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
wall-clock time is not paced: realtime_factor 0, and simulated time advances 15 minutes per step

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
